name: Tebentafusp-tebn (HLA-A*02:01+ Metastatic Uveal Melanoma)

source.textbook: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.

institution.provenance: ONCQIS Landmark Regimen: Phase III IMCgp100-202 Trial (Nathan et al. NEJM 2021)

premedications.name: IV hydration
premedications.notes: Administer before and after first 3 infusions to mitigate hypotension

supportiveCare: Inpatient observation: monitor vitals for at least 16 hours following first 3 infusions due to CRS and hypotension risk.
After dose 3 without significant CRS, subsequent infusions can be administered in an outpatient setting with 30-minute monitoring.
monitoring: Vitals every 30 minutes for 2 hours, then hourly during initial inpatient step-up infusions
CBC, CMP, liver enzymes before each cycle

doseModificationRules.condition: CRS Grade 2 (hypotension responsive to fluids, hypoxia requiring low-flow O2)
doseModificationRules.text: Administer IV fluid bolus (1-2 L), supplemental O2. Withhold infusion until resolution.
Administer tocilizumab 8 mg/kg IV and systemic steroids (dexamethasone or methylprednisolone). Consider permanent discontinuation if Grade 4.

drugs.name: Tebentafusp-tebn
drugs.notes: Tebentafusp target dose 68 mcg IV weekly (Day 15+). Step-up initiation schedule required: Day 1 (20 mcg), Day 8 (30 mcg), Day 15+ (68 mcg weekly). Grounded in IMCgp100-202 Phase III trial showing significant OS advantage in HLA-A*02:01+ metastatic uveal melanoma.
